title: R Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Show text
entries.summary: cat joins values and writes them out. A backslash-n adds a new line.
notes: Unlike print, cat does not add a new line unless you ask.

entries.name: Name a value
entries.summary: The <- arrow assigns a value to a name. Here pencils keeps the number 3.
notes: Use a number without quotes for maths.

entries.name: Keep several numbers
entries.summary: A vector is an ordered group of values. c combines values into a vector.
notes: R positions start at 1, unlike many other languages.

entries.name: Read a position
entries.summary: Square brackets select values. Position 2 is the second item in R.
notes: Index zero gives an empty selection, not the first item.

entries.name: Do maths on a vector
entries.summary: R can apply arithmetic to each value in a vector.
notes: Different vector lengths can cause recycling; check their lengths.

entries.name: Keep matching values
entries.summary: A logical test makes true-or-false values. Use them in brackets to keep matching numbers.
notes: The filter must describe the values you intend to keep.

entries.name: Find a mean
entries.summary: mean adds values and divides by their count. This is the average.
notes: Missing values need an explicit plan, such as na.rm = TRUE.

entries.name: Handle missing data
entries.summary: NA marks a missing value. is.na detects it.
notes: Do not compare with == NA; use is.na.

entries.name: Make a data table
entries.summary: A data frame stores columns of the same row count. Each column has a name.

example.code:
books <- data.frame(title = c("Moon", "Sun"), pages = c(24, 30))
cat(books$pages, "\n")

notes: Keep all columns the same length.

entries.name: Name a calculation
entries.summary: function defines reusable steps. R returns its final expression.
notes: Remember to call the function with parentheses.

entries.name: Choose a message
entries.summary: if checks one true-or-false value. else chooses the other action.

example.code:
score <- 8
if (score >= 5) { cat("Pass\n") } else { cat("Try again\n") }

notes: A whole vector is not one if condition; choose a single rule.

entries.name: Put values in order
entries.summary: sort returns a vector in order from smallest to largest by default.
notes: sort returns a result; keep it if you want to reuse it.
